solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Golf club's tip wet

parts.note: a nib is the writing tip of a pen
to lick something is to wet it with the tongue

explanation.surface: A golfer notices the end of their club is damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for an iron with a steeply angled face, roughly a nine iron.

clue.text: Arrest New York basketball player for speaking

indicators.note: for speaking means as spoken out loud, so only the sound of the word counts

parts.note: the New York Knicks are an NBA team, so a player is a Knick

explanation.surface: A New York basketball star is arrested over something he said.
explanation.walkthrough: To nick is British slang for to arrest; the silent K drops away in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police slang, to nick someone is to arrest them.

clue.text: Article on short page supporting Bob's first Wailer?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by description

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue, supporting means lying below, so the pieces before it go underneath the name's letter
first points to the opening letter of the name only

parts.note: the first letter of Bob
an is the indefinite article
a sheet of paper is a page

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about Bob Marley's first band, the Wailers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and Wailer conjure Bob Marley and the Wailers, but the wailer here is the shrieking spirit of Irish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is an Irish female spirit whose keening cry foretells a death.

clue.text: When in France, me and a lady picked up a turn of phrase

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: moi is French for me
Di, short for Diana, a lady's name

explanation.surface: A French speaker and a woman pick up a new expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests learning a phrase, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is not literal, a set turn of phrase.

clue.text: Fork out to cover party game

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting on top, so the first piece goes above the second
out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: Paying out for a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fork out' reads as paying up; the two words separate into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Korfball is a Dutch mixed-team sport like basketball, played by shooting into a high basket.

clue.text: A writer, some soldiers, and so on

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list trailing off: a writer, a few soldiers, et cetera.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' at the start looks like wordplay, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon was an English poet and memoirist famous for his First World War verse.

clue.text: Fool to be awful when entertaining His Majesty

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means having them inside your home, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to suck is slang for being very bad
HM is the abbreviation for His Majesty

explanation.surface: A clown making a hash of entertaining the King.
explanation.walkthrough: Schmuck is Yiddish-derived American slang for a fool, also spelt shmuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A shmuck is a contemptible or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Not straight with southern part of London over smell

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the London pieces sit on top of the next one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
Kew is a district of south-west London, home of Kew Gardens
a whiff is a faint smell

explanation.surface: A smell hangs over a crooked bit of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff is informal British for askew, crooked or out of line.

clue.text: City uncovered more lists

indicators.note: uncovering something strips its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: taken as written
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A city reveals more lists, as if releasing documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun for catalogues, but it is a verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a French city on the Loire, famous for Joan of Arc's siege.

clue.text: Lowest part of engine thermostat

indicators.note: part of signals that only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A mechanic points to the bottom component of an engine's thermostat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost is an old-fashioned superlative meaning lowest or farthest down.

clue.text: A small amount of cremating bungled

indicators.note: a bungled job is botched, so the letters before it end up in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Only a little of a botched cremation is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A centigram is a hundredth of a gram, a tiny unit of mass.

clue.text: Style of note female swapped with Charlie

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means one letter is taken out and a different one put in its place

parts.note: E flat is a musical note
F is the abbreviation for female
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A query about a musician's style, with a woman replaced by a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: The note is E flat; its F is replaced by C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliance or conspicuous flair, a showy style of success.

clue.text: Large creature to return carrying? Cry audibly

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy
to come back is to return

indicators.note: something done audibly is heard, so we want a word that sounds like the cry rather than one spelt like it

parts.note: a wail is a long cry

explanation.surface: A big animal comes back with a load and wails about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces come in a different order from the answer: the carrying word comes first in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The humpback is one of the largest whales, a huge marine mammal.

clue.text: A&E, say, with request to lab perhaps that's unnecessary?

definitions.note: a thing that is unnecessary, standing for the noun

parts.note: the musical interval from A up to E is a fifth
W is the abbreviation for with
heel is the command telling a dog such as a labrador to walk close

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency department asks the laboratory for something that turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's Accident and Emergency, and lab suggests a hospital laboratory, but A&E is two notes and the lab is a labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth wheel is an idiom for a superfluous person or thing, like a spare wheel no carriage needs.

clue.text: Kill American, then relax close to balcony — that's cold

definitions.note: a thing that is cold, standing for the noun

parts.note: to ice someone is US slang for killing them
to loll is to lounge about lazily

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of balcony

explanation.surface: A gangster kills someone, then lounges on a balcony: chilling behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: An ice lolly is the British name for a popsicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice lolly is frozen flavoured water on a stick, a treat served freezing cold.

clue.text: Old and stern? Not so much, and not smelly!

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
dour means severe and stern
less means not so much

explanation.surface: An old, strict person is mellowing and has stopped smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' sits next to 'Old' as if about a ship's rear, but it means severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means having no scent at all, so nothing to smell.

clue.text: Turns down occasionally yummy Asian food

parts.note: dims, as in turns down the lights

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of yummy

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes refuses delicious Asian dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns down' looks like refusing, but it means dimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Chinese dumplings and snacks served in steamers.

clue.text: Upset friends a little, being careless

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: pals are friends
a dash is a small amount, as in a dash of milk

explanation.surface: Someone has slightly upset their friends through thoughtlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like hurt feelings, but it turns the friends word over.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and carelessly, without attention to detail.

clue.text: China object to a pet exercising

indicators.note: exercising means moving about energetically, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: China objects to someone walking their pet, as if a country were protesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China object' reads as the country objecting; it is a porcelain item.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is commonly made of china, the porcelain used for tableware.

clue.text: Island worker on one other island briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker
I is the Roman numeral for one
Guam is a US island territory in the Pacific

explanation.surface: A labourer briefly works on one island and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Crawling on this is a result of poor judgement?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crawling on hands and knees
second meaning: a set of judges' marks that are all low scores of four

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a drunk crawling after a bad decision; the second half imagines judges each holding up a mediocre four.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or drunk moves on hands and knees, and a panel scoring four apiece gives a poor mark.

clue.text: Mundane novel is anonymous

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull book was published without an author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book, but here it means new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnamed has no name given, which is what anonymous means.

clue.text: Outlaw seen outside shack somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: being seen outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a hut is a shack

explanation.surface: A wanted outlaw is spotted outside a hut in an Asian land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, but it is the verb meaning to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a small Himalayan kingdom between India and China.

clue.text: Novel liquid's cool and blue

parts.note: water's, the possessive of a liquid
hip means fashionable
feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: A description of a new drink: cool and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition: a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Watership Down is Richard Adams's 1972 novel about a warren of rabbits.

clue.text: Poem about old theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on, as in a talk on a subject, means about

explanation.surface: A poem written about an ancient theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was a roofed building in ancient Greece and Rome for musical performances.

clue.text: Make out small drink containing eggs

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
nog, as in eggnog, a drink made with beaten eggs

explanation.surface: Someone tries to read a little eggnog's label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' looks like an insertion signal but is part of describing the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To snog is British slang for kissing passionately, which Americans call making out.

clue.text: Dog ignoring bone initially getting good score on course

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of bone

explanation.surface: A dog on a golf course ignores a bone and does well.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole, an excellent result.

clue.text: Shopkeeper, say, and master criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who is also a master criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master criminal' reads as one phrase, but criminal is the signal working on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper is one example of a tradesman, someone who earns a living by selling goods.

clue.text: Affair of cat eating a box of ingredients

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so these letters go within the big cat

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
taken as written

indicators.note: a box is the outside casing, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of ingredients

explanation.surface: A tale of a cat eating a whole box of cooking ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The cooking surface is apt: in the kitchen, a liaison is a thickening of egg yolk and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret love affair, especially an adulterous one.

clue.text: Spooner's dratted pig is shamefaced

indicators.note: Spooner was known for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: dang is a mild curse, like dratted, and a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A cursed pig looks ashamed of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is guilty and abject, the expression of someone ashamed.
